description: Tower-city flythrough from Hackers (1995), rendered with wgpu, as a Windows screen saver.

script: if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $scr)) { throw "Gibson.scr is missing from $dir - the release asset did not land where this manifest expects it." }
Write-Host "Gibson.scr copied to $dst, which is where Windows looks when it builds the screen saver list."
Write-Host 'A per-user install is not offered in Screen Saver Settings, which only lists savers kept in %SystemRoot%\System32; see the notes this manifest prints below.'

notes: Run it now: double-click "$dir\Gibson.scr", or from a terminal run "$dir\Gibson.scr" /s (a mouse move or Esc ends it). "/c" opens its settings file.

To select it in Windows: Settings > Personalization > Lock screen > Screen saver. That list is built from the saver files kept in %SystemRoot%\System32, so this per-user install is not shown there. Either reinstall with `scoop install -g gibson-screensaver` from an elevated shell, or copy "$dir\Gibson.scr" into %SystemRoot%\System32 as administrator - the latter is what the file's right-click Install verb does.

This manifest deliberately writes no registry values. What selects a saver is HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\SCRNSAVE.EXE, which the dialog above sets for you; Microsoft documents setting it from a file path with: rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver "$dir\Gibson.scr"
Gibson.scr is an unsigned x86_64 Rust/wgpu build, so SmartScreen may warn the first time it runs.
